title: Is Target-Based Drug Discovery Efficient? Discovery and "Off-Target" Mechanisms of All Drugs

nodes.text: A manual (non-automated) systematic review of about 32,000 articles and patents dating back 150 years was conducted to determine the discovery origins of all small-molecule drugs approved by the US FDA through the end of 2020, compiled from NCATS Inxight Drugs, Drugs@FDA, and the Orange Book.
nodes.evidence: a manual systematic review of about 32000 articles and patents dating back to 150 years ago... investigated the discovery origins of all drugs approved by the US FDA by the end of 2020

nodes.text: Only 9.4% of approved small-molecule drugs were discovered through target-based assays, despite several decades of target-based drug discovery dominance.
nodes.evidence: only 9.4% of small-molecule drugs have been discovered through "target-based" assays

nodes.text: Even the minimal share of target-based drugs cannot have their therapeutic effects solely attributed to their purported targets, because they depend on numerous off-target mechanisms incorporated unconsciously through phenotypic observations.
nodes.evidence: the therapeutic effects of even this minimal share cannot be solely attributed and reduced to their purported targets, as they depend on numerous off-target mechanisms

nodes.text: Reductionist target-based drug discovery may be a cause of the productivity crisis in drug discovery.
nodes.evidence: reductionist targetbased drug discovery may be a cause of the productivity crisis in drug discovery

nodes.text: Most disorders and desired therapeutic effects are too complex to be reducible to modulating single proteins (except perhaps monogenetic Mendelian disorders), and many hypothesized targets may not even be relevant to the phenotypes they are attributed to.
nodes.evidence: most disorders and desired therapeutic effects seem to be too complex to be reducible to modulating the behavior of single proteins, except maybe monogenetic Mendelian disorders

nodes.text: Target-based drug discovery is framed as a reductionist iteration of rational drug discovery that was born at roughly the same time as the onset of the drug-discovery productivity decline.
nodes.evidence: this methodology was born at roughly the same time as the onset of this decline and has now dominated drug discovery approaches for several decades

nodes.text: Drug discovery productivity has declined despite technological advances; from 1950 to 2010 the number of drug approvals per billion dollars of research expenditure halved every 9 years, a trend known as Eroom's Law.
nodes.evidence: the number of drug approvals per billion dollars of research expenditure has halved every 9 years, a trend referred to as Eroom's Law

nodes.text: The work extends and contrasts with Swinney and Anthony's seminal 1999-2008 analysis, which showed most first-in-class drugs in that window came from phenotypic approaches but covered too limited a period and missed the golden era of traditional drug discovery.
nodes.evidence: Swinney and Anthony showed that... most of the first-in-class drugs approved between 1999 and 2008 were discovered by phenotypic approaches... the period they analyzed (1999−2008) was so limited

nodes.text: An evidence-based path to improved efficiency is prioritizing higher-level phenotypic observations closer to the sought therapeutic effects when selecting and optimizing molecules, aided by AI and machine learning tools.
nodes.evidence: prioritizing, in selecting and optimizing molecules, higher-level phenotypic observations that are closer to the sought-after therapeutic effects using tools like artificial intelligence and machine learning

nodes.text: Several major pharmaceutical companies (Pfizer, Merck, GSK, AstraZeneca, Amgen) withdrew from neuroscience research at some point despite neurological disorders being a primary cause of disability worldwide, and drug approval rates can be as low as 0.4% for complex CNS disorders and cancers.
nodes.evidence: compelled many pharmaceutical companies, including Pfizer, Merck, GSK, AstraZeneca, and Amgen, to withdraw from neuroscience research... can be as low as 0.4% for more complex CNS disorders and cancers

nodes.text: Many crucial clinical drugs trace to therapeutics discovered by ancestors via phenotypic pattern recognition (e.g. morphine analogs, aspirin, digoxin), with intentional drug use stretching back up to 60,000 years.
nodes.evidence: some of the most crucial drugs used in the clinic can be traced back to the therapeutics our ancestors discovered centuries ago, including morphine analogs (21 drugs), aspirin, digoxin

nodes.text: This is presented as the first systematic and comprehensive assessment of the real-world efficiency of target-based drug discovery.
nodes.evidence: This is the first systematic and comprehensive assessment of the real-world efficiency of target-based drug discovery
